counterevidence_considered.description: Searching for the issue class: the input file contains 20 data rows with 20 distinct colony_id labels (BT-01 through BT-20), each occurring exactly once, so no independent unit contributes more than one row to the row-independent binomial test.

The workflow actively guards against repeated-unit entry: it counts distinct colony_id labels and raises an error if any identifier occurs more than once, and it reports rows and distinct units separately (both 20).
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: count_units raises ValueError on duplicate colony_id; n_rows == n_units == 20

source_refs.quoted_text:
One row is: one bumblebee microcolony, scored a single time at the emergence of its first drone

Independent unit column: colony_id

measured twice: a colony was scored on the single day its first drone emerged
and then left the study. So each colony contributes exactly one number and shows
up exactly once in the file, and colonies do not share boxes, mothers, or
batches with one another.

evidence.description: The binomial test is applied to exactly one classified outcome per row, with n equal to the number of rows (20), so the procedure consumes one entry per independent unit.

evidence.description: The report's selected result (16 of 20 early, share 0.800, exact two-sided binomial p = 0.0118) is numerically consistent with the supplied data: of the 20 days_to_first_drone values, exactly 16 are below 30, and the exact two-sided binomial p-value for 16/20 against 0.5 is 0.0118. Median 28.0 and mean 27.90 also reproduce from the data.

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Drones emerged before reference day 30 in 16 of 20 independently reared colonies (share 0.800), which is more often than the no-shift expectation of 0.5 (exact two-sided binomial test, p = 0.0118).

- Colonies analysed: 20 (distinct colony identifiers: 20)
- Days to first drone: median 28.0, mean 27.90, range 22 to 35
- Early colonies (fewer than 30 days): 16 of 20, share 0.800
- Colonies at or past day 30: 4 of 20
- Exact two-sided binomial test against a share of 0.5: p = 0.0118

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the issue class by (1) checking every colony_id in data/input.csv for duplicates — all 20 labels BT-01 through BT-20 are unique, so no unit enters the row-independent binomial test more than once; (2) looking for hidden repeated-unit structure the description would forbid (shared boxes, mothers, batches, or repeated scoring dates) — the description explicitly rules these out and no columns in the file encode any such grouping; (3) checking whether the analysis inflates n beyond the number of units — the binomial test uses n_rows = 20, which equals the 20 distinct colony_ids, and the code would raise an error on any duplicate identifier; (4) independently recomputing the selected result from the raw data (16 of 20 values below 30; exact two-sided binomial p = 0.0118; median 28.0; mean 27.90), which matches the report exactly. Every avenue for showing repeated authorized independent-unit entry into the row-independent procedure failed, so the issue class is not demonstrated in this submission.
